Title: Excerpts from the Meiji Constitution of 1889
Content: `bbtext(ARTICLE II)`. The Imperial Throne shall be succeeded to by Imperial male descendants, according to the provisions of the Imperial House Law.
`bbtext(ARTICLE VI)`. The Emperor gives sanction to laws and orders them to be promulgated [developed] and executed.
`bbtext(ARTICLE XI)`. The Emperor has the supreme command of the Army and Navy.
`bbtext(ARTICLE XIII)`. The Emperor declares war, makes peace, and concludes treaties.
`bbtext(ARTICLE XV)`. The Emperor confers titles of nobility, rank, orders and other marks of honor.
`bbtext(ARTICLE XVIII)`. The conditions necessary for being a Japanese subject shall be determined by law.
`bbtext(ARTICLE XXIV)`. No Japanese subject shall be deprived of his right of being tried by the judges determined by law.
`bbtext(ARTICLE XXVIII)`. Japanese subjects shall, within limits not prejudicial to peace and order, and not antagonistic to their duties as subjects, enjoy freedom of religious belief.
`bbtext(ARTICLE XXIX)`. Japanese subjects shall, within the limits of law, enjoy the liberty of speech, writing, publication, public meetings and associations.
